facts_title: What each state and stack symbol means

steps.title: The machine as a seven-tuple
steps.explain: A PDA is a finite automaton with a stack. One move reads an input symbol (or nothing: an ε-move), looks at the TOP of the stack only, and replaces that top symbol by a string. The stack is written top first.
lines: start state q0; the stack starts as Z and nothing else (Z marks the bottom)
acceptance by FINAL STATE: the input must be finished in a state of F = {q2}; the stack may hold anything
δ has 5 transitions: each one reads a symbol (or ε), looks at the top of the stack, and replaces it
table: push X on top of Z
push X on top of X

steps.title: Deterministic: both rules hold
steps.explain: Rule 1: at most one move for each (state, input symbol or ε, top of stack). Rule 2: if an ε-move is available at (state, top), there must be no reading move at that same (state, top). Rule 2 is the one people forget.
lines: rule 1 ✓  every δ(q, a, Z) has at most one element
rule 2 ✓  where an ε-move exists, at (q1, Z), no reading move is defined
so the machine never has a choice: every string has exactly one run

steps.title: Trace "aabb": the start ID
steps.explain: An ID is a complete snapshot: (state, unread input, stack). The run starts in q0 with the whole input unread and only Z on the stack.
lines: (q0, aabb, Z)

quiz.question: How many moves will accepting "aabb" take?
quiz.why: 5 moves for 4 input symbols: 2 pushes, 2 pops, 1 ε-move. The ε-moves are the ones people forget to count.

steps.title: Move 1: read a, push X on top of Z
steps.explain: In q0 with Z on top and a next in the input: δ(q0, a, Z) = (q0, XZ). The new symbols go on top, written to the LEFT of what was already there.
lines: (q0, aabb, Z)
⊢ (q0, abb, XZ)   by δ(q0, a, Z) = (q0, XZ)

steps.title: Move 2: read a, push X on top of X
steps.explain: In q0 with X on top and a next in the input: δ(q0, a, X) = (q0, XX). The new symbols go on top, written to the LEFT of what was already there.
lines: ⊢ (q0, abb, XZ)   by δ(q0, a, Z) = (q0, XZ)
⊢ (q0, bb, XXZ)   by δ(q0, a, X) = (q0, XX)

steps.title: Move 3: read b, pop X
steps.explain: In q0 with X on top and b next in the input: δ(q0, b, X) = (q1, ε). The top symbol X is removed.
lines: ⊢ (q0, bb, XXZ)   by δ(q0, a, X) = (q0, XX)
⊢ (q1, b, XZ)   by δ(q0, b, X) = (q1, ε)

steps.title: Move 4: read b, pop X
steps.explain: In q1 with X on top and b next in the input: δ(q1, b, X) = (q1, ε). The top symbol X is removed.
lines: ⊢ (q1, b, XZ)   by δ(q0, b, X) = (q1, ε)
⊢ (q1, ε, Z)   by δ(q1, b, X) = (q1, ε)

steps.title: Move 5: ε-move, leave the stack alone
steps.explain: In q1 with Z on top, reading nothing: δ(q1, ε, Z) = (q2, Z). This last ε-move is the acceptance test: it can only fire when the stack is back down to Z. Leave it out and nothing is ever accepted.
lines: ⊢ (q1, ε, Z)   by δ(q1, b, X) = (q1, ε)
⊢ (q2, ε, Z)   by δ(q1, ε, Z) = (q2, Z)
input finished ✓   q2 ∈ F ✓   →   ACCEPT
5 moves for 4 input symbols: 2 pushes, 2 pops, 1 ε-move

steps.title: Trace "abab": rejected
steps.explain: The machine has exactly one run on this string, and it does not end in an accepting configuration. A PDA need not have a move for every situation: missing transitions are how it rejects.
lines: (q0, abab, Z)
⊢ (q0, bab, XZ)   by δ(q0, a, Z) = (q0, XZ)
⊢ (q1, ab, Z)   by δ(q0, b, X) = (q1, ε)
⊢ (q2, ab, Z)   by δ(q1, ε, Z) = (q2, Z)
STUCK: there is no transition δ(q2, a, Z) and no ε-move on Z, but ab is still unread
→   REJECT

quiz.question: Before you look: is "abab" accepted?
quiz.why: It gets stuck: there is no transition δ(q2, a, Z) and no ε-move on Z, but ab is still unread.

language: { aⁿbⁿ : n ≥ 1 }: a block of a’s followed by a block of b’s of the same length.
conclusion: A deterministic PDA accepting by final state. Accepted: aabb. Rejected: abab.
